title: Decorator flow: option/argument stash params on function, command builds Command
answers: How does @click.command turn a function into a Command?
Where are @option params accumulated before the Command exists?
body:
- `decorators.py:option` → inner `decorator(f)` → `_param_memo(f, cls(param_decls, **attrs))`; returns `f` unchanged. `argument` same with `Argument`. `version_option`/`help_option`/`password_option` etc. wrap `option(...)`.
- `decorators.py:_param_memo`: if `f` is a `Command`, appends to `f.params` (option stacked above @command); else appends to `f.__click_params__` (list created on the function if missing).
- Decorators apply bottom-up, so the list is in reverse source order.
- `decorators.py:command` inner `decorator(f)`: TypeError if `f` is already a Command; starts from `attrs.pop('params')` or `[]`; reads and `del`s `f.__click_params__`, then `params.extend(reversed(...))` (explicit params= come first); defaults help to `f.__doc__`; name from `f.__name__` (lowercased, `_`→`-`, strips suffix -command/-cmd/-group/-grp); finally `cls(name=..., callback=f, params=params, **attrs)`.
- Bare `@command` works because `command` checks `callable(name)` and applies `decorator` immediately (asserts cls is None and no attrs).
- `decorators.py:group` sets `cls = Group` by default and delegates to `command`; no separate build code.
